classes.name: Z-drug hypnotics
classes.description: Zolpidem IR/ER/SL (Ambien, Ambien CR, Edluar), eszopiclone (Lunesta), zaleplon; ramelteon (Rozerem) and low-dose doxepin (Silenor) may be listed as alternatives.
classes.plainDescription: A bedtime pill for trouble falling or staying asleep.

classes.name: Orexin receptor antagonists
classes.description: Dual orexin receptor antagonists: suvorexant (Belsomra), lemborexant (Dayvigo), daridorexant (Quviviq).
classes.plainDescription: A newer bedtime pill that blocks the brain's wake signal.

classes.name: Benzodiazepines and buspirone for anxiety
classes.description: Benzodiazepines (alprazolam IR/ER, lorazepam, clonazepam, diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate) and the non-benzodiazepine anxiolytics buspirone and hydroxyzine as alternatives.
classes.plainDescription: A medicine for anxiety or panic attacks.

preferredAgent.sig: 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth at bedtime as needed, with at least 7 hours left for sleep. 5 mg is the labeled starting dose for women and adults 65+; men may start at 5 or 10 mg (label dosing).
preferredAgent.plainSig: One small pill at bedtime when needed, only if you can sleep 7 or more hours.

records.preferredRestriction: Adults only (PDL age 18+). AHCA Auto PA doc references a limit of 4 controlled substances per rolling 27 days; its scope for Z-drugs is not printed on the PDL.

alternatives.note: No PA, age 65+ (PDL p.46); listed as an alternative in the class definition

paRequired.reason: Auto PA (PDL column) (PDL p.30; AHCA Auto PA doc p.53): 10 mg needs a 10 mg fill in prior 30 days, or a 5 mg fill with 24+ day supply in prior 90 days

records.stepTherapy: Zolpidem 10 mg: trial of 5 mg required (Auto PA; AHCA Auto PA doc p.53)
records.verificationNote: Read PDL pp.30, 46. Zolpidem 5 mg listed no PA (age 18+); 10 mg Auto PA. Eszopiclone and zaleplon listed no PA (age 18+). Ramelteon listed no PA (age 65+). Not on PDL: Ambien brand 5 mg, Edluar, Lunesta brand, Silenor (doxepin 3/6 mg; only TCA doxepin capsules are listed, p.32). Controlled substance (C-IV): PDL prints no quantity or day-supply limit, none recorded. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Added the printed age limit and the controlled-substance count limit. Ramelteon is age 65+ only (already noted).]

preferredAgent.sig: 1 tablet by mouth at bedtime (standard label dosing)

records.preferredRestriction: No orexin receptor antagonist (suvorexant, lemborexant, daridorexant) is on the Florida Medicaid PDL effective 10/01/2026. This is not a confirmed exclusion: the PDL does not claim to be complete, and AHCA codes unlisted products as Non-PDL (an edit that Auto PA does not override). Confirm with AHCA whether a PA route exists.
records.verificationNote: Searched PDL pp.1-80 for suvorexant/Belsomra, lemborexant/Dayvigo and daridorexant/Quviviq: none listed. The PDL does not say it is a complete list of covered drugs, so this is treated as partial and not as a confirmed exclusion. Suvorexant is used only as the class reference drug and is not a covered pick. No alternatives listed for this class. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Reworded the restriction: absence is not proof of exclusion (the old text said 'likely excluded'). Kept noCoveredAgent with partial because no DORA is listed and no class-level coverage statement was found. Confirm with AHCA.]

preferredAgent.sig: Anxiety: 2-3 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses (e.g. 0.5-1 mg two or three times daily); usual range 1-10 mg/day. Taper to stop (label).
preferredAgent.plainSig: A small pill two or three times a day for anxiety; do not stop suddenly.

paRequired.reason: Auto PA (PDL column) (PDL p.36): brand listed Auto PA; generic clonazepam is not

records.verificationNote: Read PDL pp.30, 36, 79-80. Lorazepam 0.5/1/2 mg listed no PA (age 0+). Buspirone and hydroxyzine listed no PA, named as alternatives in the class definition. Judgment: lorazepam chosen as the benzodiazepine pick because the class is defined as benzodiazepines; buspirone is a non-controlled alternative worth considering. Controlled substance (C-IV): PDL prints no quantity or day-supply limit, none recorded. AHCA Auto PA doc has a benzodiazepine plus long-acting opioid edit (2 BZP day supply cap), not applicable to these short-acting generics. Not on PDL: clorazepate. [Sonnet check 2026-10-27: Re-verified lorazepam, alprazolam, clonazepam, diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, oxazepam, buspirone and Klonopin (Auto PA, PDL p.36) against the PDL; the controlled-substance count limit in the Auto PA doc (4 per rolling 27 days) is not printed as applying to benzodiazepines, so not recorded as a restriction.]
